observations: Large coil of stranded metal wire.
A hand holds one end of a wire showing a copper-colored core.
The exterior of the strands appears dull or oxidized.
Black tape or insulation residue is visible on the end of the strand being held.
No labels, markings, or measuring tools are visible to indicate size or quantity.

claims.claim: All sizes of bare copper wires available

risks.risk: The wire may be copper-clad aluminum (CCA) rather than solid copper.
risks.proof: A close-up video of a strand being cut or filed to show the color of the metal at the core.
A photo of the wire end next to a metric ruler or a digital caliper.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest common earthing gauge (e.g. 10mm)

risks.risk: The total quantity (weight or length) is unknown.
risks.proof: A photo of the entire coil on a weighing scale.

proof_requests: Photo of the wire cross-section next to a ruler to determine the gauge.
Photo of the coil on a weighing scale to determine the total weight.
A video of the wire being cut to confirm it is solid copper and not copper-clad aluminum.
response.reason: Copper wire is a commodity priced by weight and gauge. Neither the size of the wire nor the total weight of the coil can be determined from the photo.
